title: Decentralized Throttle & Hedge Policy — Platform Routing Notes
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This note captures a new, intentionally decentralized approach to admission control and routing for multi-region inference. The goal: keep inbound latency SLOs stable as load and GPU utilization vary, while minimizing coordination cost and preserving graceful degradation across regions.

High-level idea (one-liner):
- Each ingress / regional front proxy keeps a small, local token-bank + queue-depth wristband. Token banks are inexpensive local credits that gate accept/queue decisions. Banks are softly replenished by a regional control-plane signal and bounded by short-term forecasts of GPU capacity. Hedge lanes (fast fallback) and a lightweight circuit-breaker are used for brief bursts or when tokens are exhausted.

Why decentralized?
- Global central admission is high-latency and brittle during partitions. Most bursts are regional — local fast-path decisions reduce p50/p95 stalls and avoid cascading RPCs.

SLOs & constraints assumed here:
- Ensemble p99 tail for text-generation <= 1.2s under normal load budget.
- Background batch jobs must not starve online throughput; GPUs measured per-GPU util target = 75% (steady) with 90% hard cap to avoid thermal/memory thrash.
- Unit of admission = request tokens computed from estimated output length + model cost factor.

Signals we observe (telemetry):
- Queue depth (per-ingress, per-priority lane) sampled at 1s roll-up.
- GPU occupancy % (per-slot and per-GPU pool) at 2s roll-up.
- Active inflight KV cache size and per-request memory pressure (approx).
- Recent token-bank consumption rate (local).
- p50/p95/p99 latency for local routing and runtime slice.

Core local admission algorithm (sketch):
1) Convert request -> estimated cost units: (prompt_tokens * model_factor) + expected_generation_window.
2) Check local token-bank: if tokens >= cost -> accept immediate and debit.
3) If tokens < cost but queue_depth < queue_threshold(priority) -> enqueue in soft queue (soft-hold) and signal hedging if predicted wait > hedging_delay.
4) If tokens < cost and queue_depth >= queue_threshold -> attempt fast-fallback lane (lower-cost model variant or remote region via spillover policy) OR return 429 when no fallback available.

Token-bank semantics (differences from traditional token-bucket):
- Credits are "soft-sharded" per-tenant-class + priority band, not pure per-source. This lets us enforce fair share while keeping a compact state.
- Refill policy is controlled by control-plane heartbeat: a regional controller publishes a replenishment window (credits per-window) derived from smoothed GPU capacity forecasts and recent utilization. Refill has small jitter per-proxy to avoid sync thundering.
- Credits expire after a short TTL (e.g., 6s) to keep local decision freshness.
- Local debits are conservative: we over-estimate cost by a safety factor (1.02-1.1) to reduce oversubscription.

Queue depth adaptive thresholds:
- Static queue thresholds are bad — we derive thresholds as a function of observed GPU occupancy and recent dequeue rate. Pseudocode:
    queue_threshold = base_Q * (1 - alpha * (gpu_util_smoothed - target_util))
  where alpha is tuned per-region, base_Q chosen from capacity tests.
- For high-priority lanes (real-time conversational), threshold is raised; for background or best-effort lanes it is lowered.
- We keep a fast path to trigger hedging: if expected queueing delay exceeds hedging_delay (computed from current dequeue rate), the ingress triggers a hedged request to a fallback (local small model or remote region)._

GPU utilization smoothing & short-term forecast:
- Raw GPU util is noisy; use exponential smoothing with two windows: fast (3s) and slow (30s). Combine to form a blended util estimate used for refill windows.
- Short-term forecast: linear extrapolation from recent slope (fast window) plus a conservative cap. Forecast feeds control-plane replenishment calculations.

Cross-region spillover and fairness:
- Regions advertise spare capacity via control-plane SRs (sparse signals): %spare_slots and last-updated timestamp. Control-plane does not coordinate per-request, only publishes periodic budgets.
- Ingress uses spare budget to redirect with hedging semantics (send local request + remote only if no response in hedging_delay, or optimistic early redirect if local bank is near-zero and remote/budget advertised > threshold).
- Spillover prioritization: same-tenant, same-region > same-tenant cross-region > other-tenant. This preserves locality while allowing tenant burst absorption across regions.

Backpressure propagation & API semantics:
- Backpressure is communicated to clients conservatively: 429 with Retry-After when queueing can't help; 503 used only when runtime is in protective circuit-breaker state.
- Add a new response header X-RW-Admit-Reason with values: accepted|queued|hedged|spillover|rejected|circuit. Helps debugging and telemetry joins.

Circuit-breaker & graceful degradation:
- Circuit tracks recent error-rate + average GPU busy fraction. Enter soft-circuit if gpu_util > 92% and p99 generation latency > SLA for 30s window.
- Soft-circuit: route requests to cheap fallbacks (quantized model, cached completions, or static message) for a rolling 15s window with exponential backoff.
- Hard-circuit: reject new requests for critical tenants if continued degradation; only after operator-approved escalation.

Control-plane responsibilities (low and slow):
- Publish per-region replenishment budgets every 5–15s (tunable). Budgets computed from consolidated GPU telemetry and scheduled maintenance windows.
- Publish spare-slot advertisements for spillover.
- Provide historical telemetry and per-tenant emergency throttle knobs for SRE.
- Not responsible for per-request decisions; that stays decentralized.

Operational playbook / rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (internal canary): implement local token-bank in staging, instrument X-RW-Admit-Reason, run controlled blast tests with synthetic load across two AZs.
- Phase 2 (tenant opt-in): allow a small set of customer traffic to use hedging+spillover; monitor unit-econ changes.
- Phase 3 (global): enable for all traffic with dynamic tuning; retain toggle to fall back to current admission.

Experiment design & metrics to monitor:
- Primary: p99 end-to-end latency change, p50/p95, request acceptance rate, 429 rate, hedged request tail latency, cross-region egress cost delta.
- Secondary: GPU churn (frequency of hitting >90%), queue length distribution, token-bank exhaustion rate by tenant.
- SLO guards: if p99 tail worsens > 10% for 10m, auto-revert to previous algorithm in that region.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How accurate should local short-term forecasts be before they harm more than help? (Need experiments to vary forecast horizon.)
- Interplay with caching: cached completions should bypass token debit — ensure consistency for accounting and billing.
- Tenant burst fairness: fair-share vs priority lanes — what policies for large enterprise tenants with reserved capacity?
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs with hedging: how often will hedging increase cross-region egress cost and does that justify reduced p99?

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Spike: implement token-bank library (language: Go) used by front-proxy. (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Add X-RW-Admit-Reason header and basic telemetry fields (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Simulation harness: run multi-region synthetic traces to tune alpha, base_Q, hedging_delay (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Draft runbook entries for SRE and on-call (owner: Aisha)

Notes to self: keep the control-plane slow and explainable — avoid microsecond coordination. We want probabilistic safety (short TTL credits) rather than rigid locks. Expect many tuning iterations; start conservative.

End of note.
